source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
Branches should be pruned after each harvest. Branches that should be cut off include: old branches that no longer bear fruit, drooping/wilting branch tips, branches growing inward toward the trunk, diseased branches, and branches carrying parasitic growths. Pruning is done so the tree's health benefits, so air can circulate well through the canopy, and so the tree can produce larger fruit.

The illustration shows a before-and-after pair of trees: one full of branches (before pruning) and one with the canopy cut back (after pruning). Note: the source text gives a pruning frequency that was hard to read precisely in the scan — it appears to say pruning is done on a multi-year cycle after harvest, but the exact interval (e.g., every year vs. every few years) could not be confirmed with confidence and is not stated as a specific number here.
